blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Warehousing, at senior level, is not a cost line — it is a capability that shapes what the company can promise its customers. A warehouse designed for speed enables a different service offer than one designed for volume; a warehouse designed for flexibility supports a different product strategy than one designed for throughput. The physical building is downstream of the commercial promise, not the other way round.

Executives who understand this treat warehouse decisions as part of the product strategy. When a new customer segment opens up, the warehouse question is asked at the same time as the pricing and marketing questions — not a year later, when the building is already wrong for what the business has become.

Built on this understanding, warehousing becomes a quiet source of competitive advantage. The companies that do not understand it end up with expensive real estate holding the wrong product for the wrong customer, wondering why their unit economics refuse to improve.

items.q: According to the text, how should warehousing be understood at senior level?
options: As a cost line to be minimised
As a capability that shapes what the company can promise
As a purely operational matter for logistics teams
items.why: "it is a capability that shapes what the company can promise its customers."

items.q: What does the text mean by "the physical building is downstream of the commercial promise"?
options: The building follows from the promise, not the reverse
The promise should be designed to fit the existing building
The building determines what the company can promise
The building and the promise are unrelated
items.why: "downstream of the commercial promise, not the other way round" — a promessa vem primeiro; o prédio decorre dela.

items.q: When a new customer segment opens up, when do executives who understand warehousing ask the warehouse question?
options: A year later, once the building shows its limits
Only after pricing and marketing are settled
Once the segment has proven profitable
At the same time as the pricing and marketing questions
items.why: "the warehouse question is asked at the same time as the pricing and marketing questions."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Poor warehouse fit shows up in weak unit economics
A warehouse optimised for throughput may struggle with flexibility
Warehousing can be a quiet source of competitive advantage
Building the right warehouse is a decision that can wait until strategy is proven
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta que a decisão de warehouse deve ser feita junto com a estratégia — adiá-la é o erro que ele critica.

items.q: What does the final paragraph suggest about companies with stubbornly weak unit economics?
options: Their pricing is the only thing that needs to change
Their marketing has failed to reach the right segment
They are simply spending too little on real estate
The cause may be a warehouse mismatched to product and customer
items.why: Inferência: "expensive real estate holding the wrong product for the wrong customer, wondering why their unit economics refuse to improve" — o desencaixe do armazém é a causa implícita.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o redesenho do armazém à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me set the scene before we get into floor plans. This building was designed years ago for B2B pallets — full loads, predictable, going out by the truckload to a handful of accounts. That worked beautifully for the business we were.

But the new B2C segment behaves nothing like that. We're now picking single items, hundreds of small orders a day, each one going to a different doorstep. Trying to run that flow through a pallet-shaped building, we're seeing pick times double and errors climb. The racking, the aisles, the whole layout is optimised for exactly the wrong thing.

So I don't want us to think of this as a maintenance job — patching a warehouse. This is a strategic decision. Whatever we choose to promise these new customers on delivery speed, we can only promise it if the building can physically deliver it. Get the design wrong and we've locked in the constraint for twenty years.

My proposal is that we design the space around the service we intend to sell, not around what fits neatly on the current footprint. Give me a fortnight with the commercial team, and I'll come back with two options and the unit economics behind each.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was the original building designed for?
options: B2B pallets going out by the truckload
items.why: "This building was designed years ago for B2B pallets — full loads… going out by the truckload."

items.q: What symptoms is Emily seeing from running B2C flow through the old building?
options: Pick times doubling and errors climbing
Falling storage costs but rising rent
items.why: "we're seeing pick times double and errors climb."

items.q: Why does Emily insist this is NOT a maintenance job?
options: Because the building is too old to patch
Because the landlord has refused further changes
Because the budget is too small for repairs
Because it is a strategic decision that sets what the company can promise customers
items.why: "This is a strategic decision. Whatever we choose to promise these new customers… we can only promise it if the building can physically deliver it."

items.q: When Emily says "Get the design wrong and we've locked in the constraint for twenty years", she implies that…
options: Warehouse decisions have very long-lasting consequences
The team has twenty years to decide
The design can be easily reversed later
The lease runs for exactly twenty years
items.why: Inferência: uma escolha física de armazém amarra a operação por muito tempo — o custo do erro é estrutural, não pontual.

items.q: What does Emily's proposal reveal about how she wants to approach the redesign?
options: She wants to start from what fits the current footprint
She wants to design around the service they intend to sell
She wants to postpone the decision until sales grow
She wants to cut costs before consulting the commercial team
items.why: Inferência: "design the space around the service we intend to sell, not around what fits neatly on the current footprint" — a promessa comercial guia o prédio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "At this level, warehousing is a strategic capability, not a storage function." A capability is…
options: the power or capacity to do something well
items.why: Capability = capacidade: aquilo que a organização consegue fazer bem, e que sustenta a estratégia.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The warehouse is optimised for volume, so its raw ___ is high but same-day dispatch is impossible."
items.why: Throughput = taxa de processamento: o volume que passa pelo sistema, distinto da velocidade prometida ao cliente.

items.q: "A promise of next-day delivery is only credible if the building can honour that commercial promise." A commercial promise is…
options: what the company commits to deliver to its customers
a marketing slogan with no operational backing
items.why: Commercial promise = promessa comercial: o compromisso de serviço que a empresa assume perante o cliente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Each ___ — B2B pallets versus B2C parcels — needs a fundamentally different warehousing strategy."
items.why: Customer segment = segmento de cliente: grupos distintos que exigem operações distintas.

items.q: "Expensive real estate holding the wrong stock quietly erodes the unit economics." This sentence contrasts…
options: the physical property with the per-unit profitability
items.why: Real estate = imóveis; unit economics = economia unitária (custo/lucro por unidade). O prédio caro pesa sobre a rentabilidade por item.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre operações e reestruturação de armazéns. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the capital for the new layout." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new picking process one aisle at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the aggressive delivery target." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Redrawing the layout won't move the needle on delivery speed unless we change the racking too." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Once we commit to same-day dispatch, we have to follow through, whatever the peak-season volume." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi assumido.
